- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially if recent price action is trending up.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish or neutral (≤0.33) and recent prices show consolidation or downward momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term spikes; if price spikes followed by sentiment reversal, reduce forecast overshoot by 10–20%.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, favor lower volatility forecasts; avoid sharp upward revisions unless recent sentiment is consistently positive.
- If sentiment shows strong negative drift (e.g., -0.33 or below) in last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 5–15% to avoid overconfidence in rebound.
- Don’t assume momentum continues; if recent sentiment is weak or negative, forecast should not exceed 10% above prior 14-day high unless strong bullish sentiment persists.
